'''Jean-Claude Bradley''' was a chemist who actively promoted [[Open Science]] in chemistry,<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/455273a| title = Data on display| journal = Nature| volume = 455| issue = 7211| pages = 273| year = 2008| last1 = Bradley | first1 = J. C. | last2 = Neylon | first2 = C. | pmid=18800097}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1021/cen-v087n006.p034| title = Jean-Claude Bradley| journal = Chemical & Engineering News| volume = 87| issue = 6| pages = 34| year = 2009| last1 = Drahl | first1 = C. }}</ref> including at the [[White House]],<ref>Kirsten Vannix, Chemistry Prof Presents at the White House, 23 July 2013, {{cite web |url=http://www.drexel.edu/chemistry/news/archive/20130723/ |title=Chemistry Prof Presents at White House &#124; Department of Chemistry &#124; Drexel University |access-date=2014-05-23 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140523231016/http://www.drexel.edu/chemistry/news/archive/20130723/ |archive-date=2014-05-23 }}</ref> for which he was awarded the [[Blue Obelisk]] award in 2007.<ref name="inmem"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://blueobelisk.github.io/awards.html|title=Blue Obelisk Awards|access-date=2019-04-22}}</ref> He coined the term "[[Open Notebook science]]". He died in May 2014.<ref name="DrexelMourning"/><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://inmemoriamjcb.wikispaces.com/home |title=InMemoriamJCB - home |access-date=2014-05-23 |archive-date=2015-01-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150127063251/http://inmemoriamjcb.wikispaces.com/home |url-status=dead }}</ref> A memorial symposium was held July 14, 2014 at Cambridge University, UK.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://inmemoriamjcb.wikispaces.com/Jean-Claude+Bradley+Memorial+Symposium |title=InMemoriamJCB - Jean-Claude Bradley Memorial Symposium |access-date=2014-06-27 |archive-date=2015-01-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150123030755/http://inmemoriamjcb.wikispaces.com/Jean-Claude+Bradley+Memorial+Symposium |url-status=dead }}</ref>

One outcome of his Open Notebook work is the collection of physicochemical properties of organic compounds he was studying. All of this data he made available as [[Open data]] under the [[CCZero]] license. For example, in 2009 Bradley et al. published their work on making solubility data of organic compounds available as Open data.<ref>{{Cite book | isbn = 978-0596157111 | title = Beautiful Data: The Stories Behind Elegant Data Solutions | editor1-last = Segaran | editor1-first= Toby | editor2-last = Hammerbacher | editor2-first= Jeff | year = 2009 | publisher = O'Reilly  }}</ref> Later, the melting point data set he collaborated on with Andrew Lang and [[Antony John Williams|Antony Williams]] was published with [[Figshare]].<ref>{{Cite journal | title = Jean-Claude Bradley Open Melting Point Dataset | doi = 10.6084/m9.figshare.1031637 |last1=Bradley |first1=Jean-Claude |last2=Williams |first2=Antony |last3=Lang |first3=Andrew |website=Figshare |date=2014-05-20 |url=http://figshare.com/articles/Jean_Claude_Bradley_Open_Melting_Point_Datset/1031637}}</ref> Both data sets were also made available as books via the [[Lulu.com]] self-publishing platform.<ref>{{cite book|isbn= 9780557318018|title=Open Notebook Science Challenge: Solubilities Of Organic Compounds In Organic Solvents (3RD)|last=Lang|first=Andrew}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|isbn=9781257978045|title=Open Notebook Science Melting Point Data|last=Lang|first=Andrew|publisher=ONSBooks}}</ref>

He blogged extensively and contributed to at least 25 individual blogs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.blogger.com/profile/09157209601339686455|title = Blogger: User Profile: Jean-Claude Bradley}}</ref> In an interview in 2008 with Bora Zivkovic titled "Doing Science Publicly", he spoke of his work and online presence.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://scienceblogs.com/clock/2008/05/23/doing-science-publicly-intervi/|title=Doing science publicly: Interview with Jean-Claude Bradley &#124; ScienceBlogs}}</ref> In 2010, he gave an extensive interview about the impact of Open Notebook science with Richard Poynder.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.infotoday.com/it/sep10/Poynder.shtml|title = FEATURE: Interview with Jean-Claude Bradley - the Impact of Open Notebook Science}}</ref>
